fixes.explanation: Gifts never show up in this part, friend. Paul hopes his area of influence among them will greatly increase as their faith increases (2 Corinthians 10:15). And look where he's headed with it: "so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you." (2 Corinthians 10:16) That's a hope about the gospel reaching further, not about anything coming his way.

Good thinking, friend, but I'd put the teacher roster down. Paul hopes "…our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well…" and he ties it to their faith increasing (2 Corinthians 10:15). So it's their faith that sets the pace, not a headcount of anybody. The reason he gives is to preach the gospel in the regions beyond them (2 Corinthians 10:16).

The law is a fair guess, friend, but the verse points to a person, not a thing. Paul writes, "Let him who boasts boast in the Lord." (2 Corinthians 10:17) Then the next verse explains: "For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends." (2 Corinthians 10:18) So the boasting lands on the Lord.
